RS-S1.where: Chapter 15's wide stage at 1024 and 768 px
RS-S1.what_and_fix: Where the frame is 680 to about 760 px wide, narrow the frame's mat so the 680 px stage fits, and switch on the frame's own width as now. A few dozen bytes of shell CSS.

RS-S2.what_and_fix: Print the alt's first sentence as the visible caption, for instance "The same values with the spokes in two orders draw two different shapes; grouped bars show them as lengths from one zero."
RS-S2.owner: Maker A for 14.24, maker B for 14.45, the editor on the words

RS-S3.what_and_fix: Where the figure already draws its chips (the 1024 px column is too narrow for the grid), the "On a phone, 358 px" drawing repeats the first reform group in the same form. Show the desk phone drawing only where the figure draws a different form at that width.

RS-S4.what_and_fix: The caption says the youngest group "stands out in ink", and Rule 14.6 gives a named mark the red unless a party tie or an error holds it. Ask the data lead to rule on reported voting by age under D3-489, then draw the red point or let the caption name the case that sets ink.

judgments.chapter_15_one_column_at_1024: Its one column at 1024 px: acceptable, and it can do better. D3-625 kept the 328 px column at 1024 px because my CH15-M1 said "the narrower 1024 px column". That rested on a measure I did not check: the frame is 702 px wide at 1024 px, though its content box is 606 px. So the 680 px stage would fit if the frame's mat narrowed from 48 px to about 11 px a side, as it already does on a phone. As built, 1024 px shows the same true-size column chapters 11 and 12 show there, so it ships. Should fix RS-S1 below brings the wide composition to 1024 and 768 px. A switch at 600 px would not help: it leaves a words column about 250 px wide.
judgments.avoid_pairs: The avoid pairs: they teach. Each shows the fault and the cure from the same invented values, side by side, and only the misleading half carries the bar. The visible caption still reads only "Radar chart, drawn small with illustrative data."; RS-S2 gives it the one sentence the alt already has.
judgments.rule_14_6_national_parks: Rule 14.6 on national parks: the right example. No reader ties a park's visits to a party, so the red point the rule teaches carries no second meaning. The count is documented, and Great Smoky Mountains leads Zion by 2.3 times, a margin that shows at once. The source line says the count is of visits, not people, and of national parks only. The rule's text has grown a list of party ties; risk R1 below.
judgments.s37_over_the_share: S37 at 16 KB, over the share: accept it. Its chart weighs 16,253 bytes against the 14,337 share, and its entry 20,499 with words. It is an extended form drawing 126 cells for 50 reforms; the far-over test allows it, and the desk phone drawing adds no data (D3-554). Round 1's new entries have a median of 12,584 bytes, about 1.75 KB under the share, so the pool absorbs it. S37 now runs 5,427 px tall at 1440 px; the 1024 px repeat in RS-S3 is the one part to trim.

weight_recommendation.verdict: Holds: round 1’s new entries sit about 1.75 KB under the share at the median, which absorbs S37; little margin is left for round 3’s maps and distributions.

distinctiveness_test.view: Chapter 14, opener in view at 1440 px, wordmark covered
distinctiveness_test.verdict: Now reads as Oath & Action: sixteen small drawn marks in the house line beside Inter Tight questions.

distinctiveness_test.view: Chapter 15, any wide plate at 1440 px
distinctiveness_test.verdict: Reads as Oath & Action: typed chips, the line code with its ticks, lettered callouts and the legend beside the drawing.
Reads as Oath & Action: one red bar inside its keyline, every other bar in the light fill.

risks_for_dustin: The party test is spreading. D3-489 lists five ties, and the studio has applied it well, but 14.12's 2026 receipts column takes ink because the year's receipts carry the sitting president's tariffs (D3-589), a reason outside the list. Applied that broadly, red becomes rare, and the reason given is itself a political reading. I recommend the data lead keep the test to the list Rule 14.6 prints, and add a case to the rule before using it.

Where readers learn the red point. Most entries that draw it now draw the atlas's own records (S21, S23). Rule 14.6's park plate shows it on public data; a later round should add one entry specimen like it.

Margin. Chapter 14's share is 14,337 bytes for each of 61 plates, with sketch entries reserved whole. Round 1's median sits about 1.75 KB under it, which leaves little for round 3's maps and distributions.
